reasoning: The baseline Random Forest (cv=0.69) and the previous voting ensemble (iter01_c1, cv=0.71) showed promise but suffered from high train/test gaps or suboptimal regularization. Evidence 'ev_5294c787c1645c' supports combining LR and RF with soft voting. Evidence 'ev_67cadb757a26d2' suggests RFE for feature selection in high-dimensional tabular data. To improve generalization on this small dataset (n=1252, n_features=49), we propose: 1) A refined Soft Voting ensemble using Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression with tuned regularization (C=0.1) to combat overfitting, addressing the gap seen in iter01_c2. 2) An RFE-based Pipeline using a single Random Forest model to reduce dimensionality before prediction, leveraging evidence 'ev_67cadb757a26d2' and the known benefit of feature selection on small samples.

This tests if boosting complements linear models better than previous attempts and reduces overfitting risks on small data.

Implement Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) within a pipeline to reduce the 49 features, addressing the high dimensionality challenge noted in evidence 'ev_67cadb757a26d2'. Using a single Random Forest with tuned depth and leaf size after selection aims to minimize overfitting compared to the baseline.
